Definition: a primary verb; to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill):--eat, taste.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says geúomai, it means eat, taste. The word appears 15 times, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that geúomai matters because God invites us to taste and see that He is good — faith is not blind. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
